problemStatement.formal: Resolve the finiteness of Beurling prime counting and connect the ordinary prime sequence to the Beurling-prime abstraction.
problemStatement.plain: Show that the Beurling counting function is finite in the formal model and that ordinary primes instantiate the abstraction.
whyMatters: The result removes a small infrastructure gap in the Beurling-prime formalization.
It gives a verified bridge between generalized prime systems and the usual prime-counting function.

proven: beurlingPi_finite proves the finite-counting fact for Beurling prime sequences.
primeSeq_isPrime, primeSeq_strictly_increasing, and primeSeq_gt_one establish ordinary primes as a valid sequence.
primeSeq_well_separated proves the ordinary prime sequence satisfies the well-separated-products condition.
actualPrimes packages ordinary primes as a BeurlingPrimes structure.
actualPrimes_counting proves that Beurling counting agrees with primePi for ordinary primes.
erdos_951_primes_equality records the bridge theorem between the generalized and ordinary counting functions.
open: The broader erdos951_conjecture is explicitly left open and is not axiomatized.
knownResults.goal: Document the completed Beurling-prime counting infrastructure while keeping the larger conjecture out of scope.
